[Task index](core.md) · [Canvas](drawing.md) · [Audio and saves](audio-save.md)

Start with AssetCollection for related embedded images, fonts and sheets.
It owns decoded values and copied atlas metadata. Successful loads return
stable borrowed pointers, even as later loads grow the collection. Encoded
bytes are borrowed only for the synchronous load. Release the collection once;
do not individually deinit returned resources or copy a live owner.

| Source-local name in a signature | Public game import |
| --- | --- |
| image_module.Image / image_module.DecodeOptions | [`up.assets.Image`](#assets-Image) / [`up.assets.ImageDecodeOptions`](#assets-ImageDecodeOptions) |
| font_module.Font / font_module.LoadOptions | [`up.assets.Font`](#assets-Font) / [`up.assets.FontLoadOptions`](#assets-FontLoadOptions) |
| atlas_module.Atlas / atlas_module.FrameSpec | [`up.assets.Atlas`](#assets-Atlas) / [`up.assets.AtlasFrameSpec`](#assets-AtlasFrameSpec) |
| Atlas.DecodeOptions | [`up.assets.Atlas.DecodeOptions`](#assets-Atlas-DecodeOptions) |
| atlas.AtlasFrameHandle | [`up.assets.AtlasFrameHandle`](#assets-AtlasFrameHandle) |

Options referring to source-local enums can use inferred literals:
DrawSpriteOptions.origin accepts `.top_left` or `.center`; its sampling accepts
`.nearest` or `.linear`. Defaults are shown with the declarations.

Load during init, reuse during update/draw, and deinit during game cleanup.
Use `errdefer self.deinit(ctx) catch {}` before fallible initialization so
partial loads are cleaned up. A failed load leaves prior resources valid.
The [complete workbench](../../examples/asset_workbench_game.zig) demonstrates
that lifecycle; these smaller examples are actual tests from the
[compiled recipe module](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig).

## First image

The module imports std and up and embeds its local examples/assets fixtures.
When copying into an independent project, use your own asset paths within the
module root as explained in [image setup](../guides/image-assets.md).

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L44) (`test: recipe: draw an embedded image`):

```zig
test "recipe: draw an embedded image" {
    var assets = up.assets.AssetCollection.init(std.testing.allocator);
    defer assets.deinit();
    const image = try assets.image(@embedFile("assets/ball.png"), .{});
    var canvas = try up.graphics.Canvas.init(std.testing.allocator, 16, 16);
    defer canvas.deinit();
    canvas.clear(up.core.Color.transparent);
    canvas.drawImage(image.*, 0, 0);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(up.core.Color.rgb(255, 198, 74), canvas.get(8, 8).?);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(up.core.Color.transparent, canvas.get(0, 0).?);
}
```


## Authored font

Font rasterizes the configured codepoint ranges at load time. Defaults are
shown under FontLoadOptions below; range selection and atlas size affect
memory and missing-glyph behavior. UTF-8 decoding does not provide shaping,
bidirectional layout, font fallback chains or dynamic glyph loading.

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L56) (`test: recipe: draw an authored font`):

```zig
test "recipe: draw an authored font" {
    var assets = up.assets.AssetCollection.init(std.testing.allocator);
    defer assets.deinit();
    const font = try assets.font(@embedFile("assets/fonts/Basic-Regular.ttf"), .{
        .pixel_height = 12,
        .atlas_width = 128,
        .atlas_height = 128,
        .first_codepoint = 32,
        .codepoint_count = 96,
    });
    var canvas = try up.graphics.Canvas.init(std.testing.allocator, 64, 20);
    defer canvas.deinit();
    canvas.clear(up.core.Color.transparent);
    font.drawText(&canvas, "Peas 42", 1, 1, up.core.Color.white);
    // Same authored-font golden as the pre-collection native/Wasm decoder.
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u64, 6_940_701_260_184_702_440), up.testSupport.canvasHash(canvas));
}
```


### Proportional measurement and prepared paragraphs

Use `font.measureText(text, .{})` to get authored advances, line boxes and
glyph bounds without allocating. `font.layoutText(allocator, text, options)`
creates an owned `Font.TextLayout`; draw it repeatedly through `layout.draw`.
The layout borrows an unchanged, stable Font and must be released first.
Input text is consumed during preparation and can then be freed.

The [menu/dialogue example](../../examples/font_layout_game.zig) prepares
labels and paragraphs in init. Its field definitions and source constants
are in the complete compiled module:

[Compiled source](../../examples/font_layout_game.zig#L21) (`Game.init`):

```zig
pub fn init(self: *Game, ctx: *up.core.GameContext) !void {
    const allocator = try ctx.requireAllocator();
    self.assets = up.assets.AssetCollection.init(allocator);
    errdefer self.deinit(ctx) catch {};
    // Collection pointers are stable even if its registry or Game moves.
    self.font = try self.assets.?.font(@embedFile("assets/fonts/SourceSans3-Regular.otf"), .{ .pixel_height = 14 });
    const font = self.font.?;
    self.title = try font.layoutText(allocator, "Lantern Post", .{ .max_width = 304, .alignment = .center });
    for (labels, &self.menu) |label, *target| target.* = try font.layoutText(allocator, label, .{ .max_width = 100, .alignment = .center, .wrap = .none });
    for (pages, &self.dialogue) |text, *target| target.* = try font.layoutText(allocator, text, .{ .max_width = 156, .line_spacing = 2 });
    self.hint = try font.layoutText(allocator, "UP/DOWN: choose   SPACE: next clue", .{ .max_width = 304, .alignment = .center });
}
```


See [authored text layout](../guides/authored-text-layout.md) for advance versus
glyph bounds, exact space/newline/oversized-word behavior, limits, errors and
native/Wasm commands. New nested Font.TextOptions/TextMetrics/TextLayout and
measureText/layoutText methods are additive. Existing Font.drawText and the
debug-font graphics.layoutText/TextLayout retain their behavior.

## Atlas animation

Frames and the clip below are static game-owned definitions. The atlas owns
copied frame metadata and image data; player/clip reference handles, not owned
pixels. SpriteAnimationPlayer borrows its clip and steps, so those must outlive
the player. Call advance from fixed update, not draw.

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L6) (`frames`):

```zig
pub const frames = [_]up.assets.AtlasFrameSpec{
    .{ .name = "left", .x = 0, .y = 0, .w = 8, .h = 16 },
    .{ .name = "right", .x = 8, .y = 0, .w = 8, .h = 16 },
}
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L10) (`steps`):

```zig
pub const steps = [_]up.graphics.SpriteAnimationStep{
    .{ .frame = .{ .index = 0 }, .ticks = 6 },
    .{ .frame = .{ .index = 1 }, .ticks = 6 },
}
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L14) (`clip`):

```zig
pub const clip = up.graphics.SpriteAnimationClip{ .steps = &steps, .mode = .loop }
```

[Compiled source](../../examples/asset_recipes.zig#L74) (`test: recipe: advance animation only in fixed update and draw an atlas frame`):

```zig
test "recipe: advance animation only in fixed update and draw an atlas frame" {
    var assets = up.assets.AssetCollection.init(std.testing.allocator);
    defer assets.deinit();
    const atlas = try assets.atlas(@embedFile("assets/ball.png"), &frames, .{});
    try clip.validateForAtlas(atlas);
    var player = try up.graphics.SpriteAnimationPlayer.init(&clip);
    var canvas = try up.graphics.Canvas.init(std.testing.allocator, 8, 16);
    defer canvas.deinit();
    player.advance(6);
    canvas.clear(up.core.Color.transparent);
    canvas.drawAtlasFrame(atlas.*, player.currentFrame(), 0, 0, .{});
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 1), player.currentFrame().index);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(up.core.Color.rgb(255, 198, 74), canvas.get(0, 8).?);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(up.core.Color.transparent, canvas.get(7, 0).?);
}
```


Decode/collection operations can fail with allocation errors or invalid/
unsupported content: representative errors include `InvalidImage`,
`ImageTooLarge`, `InvalidFontData`, `InvalidAtlas`, `DuplicateAtlasFrame`
and `UnknownAnimationFrame`. Animation's explicit Error set appears below;
validate clips against their atlas before play. See the
[image/font guide](../guides/image-assets.md) for full format/limit behavior.

Direct Image/Font/Atlas values remain independently owned and require deinit.
Image.sprite returns a borrowed view of image pixels; clones are separate
owners. Frame handles only make sense with their matching atlas.
Collection cleanup does not unload Audio-host resources.

## `up.assets.AssetCollection`

[Source declaration](../../src/asset_collection.zig#L11).

Optional game-owned collection of decoded embedded assets. Returned
pointers remain stable as the collection grows and borrow its lifetime.
Do not deinit them individually or copy a live collection into two owners.
Encoded bytes are borrowed only during each synchronous load. Audio and
native runtime-file loading retain their existing, separate ownership.

<a id="graphics-SpriteAnimationClip"></a>
## `up.graphics.SpriteAnimationClip`

[Source declaration](../../src/sprite_animation.zig#L24).

Immutable, game-owned sprite-frame animation data.

A clip borrows its step slice, so a game will normally declare the steps
as `const` static data and store the clip by value. It owns no image, Atlas,
renderer, clock, or allocation. Validate it once before constructing a
player.

[`Error`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationClip-Error) · [`init`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationClip-init) · [`validate`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationClip-validate) · [`validateForAtlas`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationClip-validateForAtlas) · [`totalTicks`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationClip-totalTicks)

Fields, variants and defaults (methods follow):

```zig
struct {
    steps: []const SpriteAnimationStep,
    mode: SpriteAnimationMode = .loop,
}
```

<a id="graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer"></a>
## `up.graphics.SpriteAnimationPlayer`

[Source declaration](../../src/sprite_animation.zig#L74).

Mutable, value-semantic playback state for one `SpriteAnimationClip`.

Call `advance(1)` from every fixed-step `Game.update`, then use
`currentFrame()` with the ordinary Atlas/Canvas draw API. Copying a player
copies its independent playback state; neither the player nor its clip
allocates in update or draw paths.

[`init`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-init) · [`play`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-play) · [`pause`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-pause) · [`resumePlayback`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-resumePlayback) · [`restart`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-restart) · [`isPaused`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-isPaused) · [`isCurrentClip`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-isCurrentClip) · [`isFinished`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-isFinished) · [`currentStepIndex`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-currentStepIndex) · [`currentFrame`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-currentFrame) · [`advance`](#graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-advance)

Fields, variants and defaults (methods follow):

```zig
struct {
    clip: *const SpriteAnimationClip,
    step_index: usize = 0,
    ticks_in_step: u32 = 0,
    paused: bool = false,
    complete: bool = false,
    cycle_ticks: u64,
}
```

<a id="graphics-SpriteAnimationPlayer-advance"></a>
### `up.graphics.SpriteAnimationPlayer.advance`

[Source declaration](../../src/sprite_animation.zig#L138).

Advances an exact number of simulation ticks. This never reads a wall
clock and does not mutate rendering state. Large loop advances skip
complete cycles rather than iterating one tick at a time.

```zig
pub fn advance(self: *SpriteAnimationPlayer, ticks: u32) void;
```



The older `assets.AnimationPlayer` remains supported; use the tick-based
SpriteAnimationPlayer above for new deterministic games. Neither API adds
movement, collision or a scene graph.
